Emma S: Hey team — running a POC kick tomorrow with Atlantic Retail. Need a quick handoff: they want streaming chat + function/tool calls for inventory lookups, structured JSON outputs for downstream ETL, and a webhook fallback. Can we confirm SDK patterns and any known gaps?
Jordan (DevEx): Got it. Main things to confirm: websocket vs SSE for streaming, auth methods for webhooks (signed headers / short-lived creds), and an example of function calling pattern.
Mia (Presales): Customer asks whether we support 2-step handshake for webhooks (verify + ack) and replay protection. Also wants rough pricing delta if they move from hosted to Dedicated at ~200 req/s.
Raj (Eng Platform): For streaming we recommend WebSocket for bi-directional (sync tool calls), SSE is okay for uni-directional stream to client. Our SDKs (js/py/go) have streaming client helpers. Known caveat: older node SDK versions had a bug with backpressure; update to >=1.12.2.
Jordan (DevEx): Quick snippet for function call flow we give:
```
// client sends prompt with `tool_call` allowed
await client.chat.stream({
  model: 'rw-text-1',
  input: prompt,
  allow_tools: ['inventory_lookup']
});
// server receives tool_call event, executes lookup, returns structured JSON result
```
Use structured schema validation on the tool side.
Lucas (Security): For webhooks we require either mTLS + signed header (HMAC) or short-lived creds via our connector. Replay protection: include a timestamp + nonce in the signature and reject >5m drift. They should also IP-allowlist our egress if using Dedicated/Private.
Nina (Infra): On the Dedicated pricing — 200 req/s with streaming and tool calls is throughput-heavy. Ballpark: recommend a committed pool 4x the baseline due to KV cache and concurrency; I'll DM exact #s. Also note GPU quantization changes unit cost.
Tom (CS): They specifically want the structured output to match their ETL schema (inventory.{sku,qty,loc,timestamp}). We can supply a schema validator in the runbook and example prompt templates. They also asked about ordering guarantees for events.
Raj (Eng Platform): Ordering: streaming over WebSocket preserves server-to-client message order. If they fan out to multiple downstream consumers, recommend a sequence id in the payload. We also support per-request client-provided dedup keys.
Jordan (DevEx): Webhook handshake example we give:
```bash
# on our side: POST /webhook/register -> returns ephemeral_secret
# later events: headers X-RI-Timestamp, X-RI-Signature (sha256(secret + body + ts))
curl -H "X-RI-Timestamp: 1618880000" -H "X-RI-Signature: sha256=..." -d '{"event":...}' https://customer.example/webhook
```
Emma S: Useful. Any SDK helper for computing/validating signatures? Customer is using Java/Scala microservices.
Jordan (DevEx): JS/py already have helpers; Java is on our backlog but there is an internal util in platform we can expose. For now share the sample HMAC code (Java):
```java
Mac mac = Mac.getInstance("HmacSHA256");
mac.init(new SecretKeySpec(secret.getBytes(), "HmacSHA256"));
byte[] sig = mac.doFinal((timestamp + body).getBytes());
```
Mia (Presales): Ok to promise short-lived creds for webhook? They want token rotation handled by us.
Lucas (Security): We can offer ephemeral tokens via the connector (STS-like) for Dedicated and Private. For hosted, we issue static secrets but support rotation via API. Document this clearly in the security questionnaire.
Nina (Infra): Note network egress: if they insist on webhook over private network, recommend Private deployment (VPC) else use mutual TLS + IP allowlist for hosted.
Tom (CS): For the POC checklist — need: sample schema, webhook handshake example, Java HMAC snippet, SDK version matrix, and a small perf runbook for 200 req/s. Can someone assemble a short pack?
Jordan (DevEx): I'll assemble the pack (2 slides + code samples + runbook). Will include SDK matrix and known node bug note. ETA 2 hours. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Raj (Eng Platform): I'll add platform caveats (quantization, KV cache sizing, ordering/dedup keys).
Lucas (Security): I'll write the security bits and the questionnaire answers (we'll flag mTLS + ephemeral tokens as recommended).
Nina (Infra): I'll produce a Dedicated rough capacity estimate and note the cost delta vs hosted.
Emma S: Thanks — can we also call out function/tool call timeout behavior? They will call external inventory API which may take ~1s and occasionally 5-10s.
Raj (Eng Platform): Tool execution: synchronous tool calls block the generator until result or timeout. Default tool timeout = 10s but can be configured per-route. For long ops, recommend async callback pattern: return 202 with job id then send result via webhook when done.
Tom (CS): If they prefer single-stream UX, we can do optimistic partial responses and then patch in final tool result via a follow-up event. We've done that for other retailers.
Emma S: Great. Last Q — any pitfalls for structured JSON enforcement? They will require strict typing.
Jordan (DevEx): Pitfalls: model hallucination fields, numeric vs string types, and schema drift. Mitigations: strong prompt anchoring, few-shot examples, and an output validator that rejects non-conformant responses (we include in the runbook).
